The project's current-state entrypoint was read for method and gate state only. The implementation review, evidence manifest, integration review, review packet, readings and ledgers are not curated on this subject and are not evidence here. Gumi is Narita, not Haruka. assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The dossier's governing account is an interpretive hypothesis: ease as an end that sometimes requires competent action, with money, flexible time, rest, ordinary company and minimum self-support as its positive content (sections 1, 3, 8 and 9, NT-E01 to E07); the model operationalizes it as NM1 to NM5 behind identity, obligation and represented-alternative gates and forbids a laziness score or numerical cost minimizer. C is rejected because the dossier says the evidence shows no explicit ordering or policy that predicts every case, her whole biography is unavailable, and the model is weaker when choosing between newly balanced alternatives. E is rejected because the account is corroborated across fresh V04, V05, V06.5, V07 and V08 windows and tested against six named rival readings (section 10).

The model's five selectors (NT04_WORK_ADVICE, NT05_QUIET_SHIFT, NT65_FRIEND_OUTING, NT07_FESTIVAL_VISIT, NT08_FUTURE_TALK) and the dossier's source-position table keep the episodes distinct, refuse an NT12 behavior state, and require an era-selection request for 'late series Narita'. C is rejected because the dossier describes an orientation tested and refined rather than changed, with no crisis arc or developmental transition, nothing after V08 supplies conduct, V06 is an inherited route, and the selectors are encounter contexts rather than modeled state transitions. E is rejected because explicit era selectors with stated non-transfer exceed an undifferentiated profile.

The discovery row does not claim SPEECH. The dossier notes teasing metaphors and drawn-out or relaxed represented speech and the model permits only informal, playful or slack register where the local relationship supports it, while stating that no dependable idiolect is established, broad speech testing was not performed and no audio was inspected; it forbids fabricating an attested sentence. D is rejected because her diction is characterized only at that level of generality; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the recipient-specific communicative acts are located (V04 p-0015 teasing welcome, V06.5 part0045 address refusal, V07 part0023 banter).

Ordinary life is her best-documented domain: job selection by pay, burden and shift flexibility (V04 p-0015), routine order coordination and coordinated glass washing (V04 p-0013 P324-346, V05 part0012 P324-355), shopping with named friends, heat, fatigue, rest and the detour decision (V06.5 part0041), and a relaxed festival visit (V07 part0023); NM1 and NM2 operate on these and the model names routine work and familiar play among its firmer fields. B is rejected because home, family, education and household management are unshown, the dossier refuses to infer favorite drinks or brand identity from single objects, and the episodes are few. D is rejected because several fresh, paragraph-located ordinary scenes carry a modeled mechanism.

The dossier's section 9 recipient row separates playful advice to Fumiya, familiar but selectively refusing exchanges with Mizusawa Takahiro, impatient leading of hesitant friends (Mamiya Yoko, Fujii Hitomi) and V07 banter with Nakamura, and NM4 requires the actual relationship and audience. C is rejected because each recipient rests on one or two scenes, the dossier says the friends do not supply independent psychologies and that conduct with strangers, managers or family is not established, and the model weakens on unseen recipient reactions. E is rejected because recipient-specific variation is located and explicitly bounded.

Her reasons are rendered through her own located self-reports (the V04 job criteria and cost/return account, the V08 anti-dependence reasoning) and through the V06.5 unit's narration of her comparative reasons for resisting and then leading the detour (dossier section 5). C is rejected because access is confined to these local cost reasons, motive beyond stated reasons remains OPEN, and the dossier rejects any separate hidden self. E is rejected because her reasons are directly stated or narrated in located windows rather than only inferred by an observer.

Only low-stakes disagreements are located: resisting and then leading the V06.5 detour, declining the given-name invitation in one teasing bar exchange (V06.5 part0045 P18-54), and rejecting Fumiya's challenge-centered life and his common-premise synthesis (V08 part0032 P81-127). D is rejected because no dispute beyond mild disagreement is shown and the dossier and model state that response under severe unfamiliar stress is unknown; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because these located disagreements and the explicit high-stakes limit are characterized.

Ethically relevant conduct is located but not deliberated: the V05 unasked relay of Fumiya's consultation to Mizusawa, her refusal to claim knowledge of Konno's particular desire (V04 p-0015), and the V08 independence concern, which is practical prudence rather than moral reasoning. The fairness and permission distinctions are the dossier's VALUE JUDGMENTS and the model's constraints. D is rejected because she states no ethical position; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the relay's information cost and its limits are explicitly characterized.

Comic self-presentation and teasing recur across fresh windows: the comic no-desire persona and teasing welcome (V04 p-0015), teasing the Mizusawa brothers and the shared-surname joke (V06.5 part0045), teasing Mizusawa about his presentation and relationship status (V07 part0023), and the comic wealthy-spouse answer (V08 part0032); NM4 admits play with known recipients. C is rejected because play is characterized only as a comic low-effort persona and teasing with known recipients, with no complete play style or idiolect and no evidence for unfamiliar recipients. E is rejected because the pattern is corroborated across four volumes.

The B-scope dossier disclaims mature-monograph breadth and exhaustive occurrence indexing. NT-E01 to E07 are fresh paragraph-located primary windows in V04, V05, V06.5, V07 and V08; NT-E08 (V06 and the V12 cast sheet) is inherited analytical and paratext evidence; unrequested V06.5 gaps were not read; no images or audio were inspected; other unrepresented volumes are not absence findings. C is rejected because this is a bounded dossier, not specialist interpretation at monograph strength; E is rejected because it is independently reviewed with fresh located returns across five volumes and paired with a dedicated accepted model.

Both items state affirmative limits: she declines to pretend to know Konno's exact desire; the V05 relay is not a known secrecy breach and Fumiya's concern stays inward; teasing is not romance and the bar drinks are explicitly nonalcoholic; the wealthy-spouse wish carries an explicit anti-dependence limit; she does not agree to Fumiya's synthesis; Gumi is Narita, not Haruka, and Mamiya Yoko is not Hinami Yoko; and six named rival readings fail (dossier sections 2, 4, 6-8, 10; model negative checks). B is rejected because each limit rests on one scene; D is rejected because located, scene-specific limits exceed bare gap statements.

Claims are bound to volume, member and paragraph windows (NT-E01 to E07), the V06.5 units are held at their story-local mixed clock with the bar story's seam explicitly left open, the V12 cast sheet is denied behavioral status, and the model withholds source-local facts from an earlier actor. B is rejected because the V06.5 seam is unresolved, nothing after V08 has a selector, and the selectors carry encounter context rather than knowledge transitions; D is rejected because claims are bound to exact eras and clocks, not a loose period.

scenario_readiness.note: The model returns communicative acts and register constraints, not exact dialogue by default, forbids fabricating attested sentences, and states that idiolect is unestablished, broad speech testing was not performed and no audio was inspected. CONDITIONAL would generate speech from register labels; NOT_ASSESSED would ignore the located communicative acts.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One of the selectors NT04_WORK_ADVICE, NT05_QUIET_SHIFT, NT65_FRIEND_OUTING (V06.5 at its story-local clock), NT07_FESTIVAL_VISIT or NT08_FUTURE_TALK within Japanese V04-V08; the V12 cast sheet supplies no behavior and nothing after V12 is established.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Only attested recipients in their represented standing: Fumiya as one-year-older coworker and advice seeker, Mizusawa Takahiro as familiar coworker, the Mizusawa brothers and bar staff, her friends Mamiya Yoko and Fujii Hitomi, and the V07 festival acquaintances including Nakamura.
setting_constraints: Familiar karaoke part-time workplace, low-stakes peer leisure and casual advice or future-preference talk only
No severe unfamiliar crisis, sustained demanding labor, household or financial planning, adult partnership, family or education field
Represented alternatives, fatigue and obligation must be supplied; no numerical cost optimization

scenario_readiness.note: The model returns hypothetical ranges only inside its familiar low-stakes selectors, says confidence is weaker for unseen recipient reactions and newly balanced alternatives, and places family, education, demanding labor, severe crisis, adult partnership and finances out of distribution. CONDITIONAL is rejected because a materially novel context is precisely where the evidence thins and the selectors end at V08; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the model explicitly bounds hypothetical use.

conditions: Only near analogs of the V06.5 outing or V07 visit with the attested friends or familiar acquaintances, under one named selector.
Fatigue, alternatives and the cost of resisting or reversing must be supplied; continued reluctance and initiative both remain possible.
Teasing is not read as romance and familiarity is not universal informality; casual information relay is flagged as a possible permission cost.
No invented preferences, routines or biography; behavior is described in prose and no quoted speech is generated as canonical.
scenario_readiness.note: NM2 and NM4 with dossier sections 5 and 6 support familiar peer leisure and relaxed exchanges with known recipients, which the model names among its comparatively firmer fields. READY is rejected because this rests on a story-local outing, one bar scene and one festival visit and the dossier refuses universal sociability; NOT_READY would deny the located, model-admitted ordinary company.

No ethical reasoning of hers is rendered; the model refuses to guarantee discretion or a confidentiality practice and stops on private motive. CONDITIONAL would invent deliberation; NOT_ASSESSED would ignore the located relay and the stated limits.

No romantic episode of hers is located; the dossier rejects reading teasing as attraction, the wealthy-spouse wish is a stated preference with no partner, and adult partnership is out of distribution. CONDITIONAL would generate romantic conduct without evidence; NOT_ASSESSED would ignore the explicit limits.

conditions: Only a familiar routine karaoke shift with known coworkers (NT04_WORK_ADVICE or NT05_QUIET_SHIFT), with ordinary task obligations still applying.
An ease preference is never converted into nonperformance of a task she is shown doing, and competence is not read as love of work.
No customer crisis, sustained demanding labor, supervisory role, career choice or earnings claim.
Output is a qualitative prose range with assumptions and unknowns, not generated canonical dialogue.
scenario_readiness.note: NM1 with NT-E01 to E03 supports routine part-time work: chosen criteria, order coordination and coordinated glass washing during a quiet shift, which the model names among its firmer fields. READY is rejected because only two work windows exist and exceptional service, management, customer crises and any career are unshown; NOT_READY would deny the located, model-admitted routine shift.

known_limits.statement: In the V04 consultation (p-0015 P1-86) she declines to claim Konno's particular desire; her general cost/return account does not supply a specific person's motive.

Her V05 relay of Fumiya's consultation to Mizusawa (part0012 P324-355) is not shown as breaking a known secrecy agreement, Fumiya's concern stays inward, and no confidentiality rule follows; it shows that easy circulation can outpace permission.
Teasing Mizusawa or the brothers is not attraction to every man, the V06.5 bar drinks are explicitly nonalcoholic, and no adult experience is inferred.
The V08 wealthy-spouse wish is paired with a stated need for minimum self-support (part0032 P81-127); no actual partner, wealth, occupation or financial plan is established.
Gumi is Narita's permitted workplace nickname, not Hinami Haruka, and her friend Mamiya Yoko is not Hinami Yoko.
The V12 cast sheet identifies her but supplies no conduct; the model has no NT12 behavior state and requires era selection for late-series requests.
Family, home and education history, sustained demanding labor, severe unfamiliar crisis, adult partnership, finances and an enduring confidentiality practice are unknown.
The historical seam of the V06.5 bar story is unresolved and unrequested V06.5 gaps were not read.
The V06 route is inherited without a fresh reread; the readings, ledgers, implementation and integration reviews and the evidence packet are not curated on this subject.
No idiolect, stable phrasing or acoustic manner is established and generated speech was not evaluated.
